AccountCreationConfirmationV1.description:
An opaque server-owned creation decision. Verified provider claims never
cross this boundary; the same original client must redeem the authority.

AccountCreationResponseV1.description:
A race returns the decision which actually committed, including a confirmed
continuation when cancellation arrived too late. It never claims erasure.

AccountErrorCode.description: Stable append-only error token; unknown valid tokens remain errors.

AddGoogleCandidateId.description:
Opaque, one-use authorization candidate produced by a verified provider
callback. Its contents are server-owned and must never be logged.

verified_email.description: Display-only provider-verified email. It is never an authorization key.

AppConnectionListResponseV1.description:
`GET /v1/account/connections`: every connection, live and revoked, and the
account's active Profiles, so a list can name each connection's Profiles
and offer the ones it has no decision for.

profiles.description: Every active Profile of the account, read as consent reads them.

workspaces.description:
Grants pinned to a Workspace UUID (root-catalog Plan 3.3); empty for
a connection approved before them.

AppConnectionWorkspaceGrantV1.description:
The person's choice for one Workspace, pinned to its UUID (root-catalog
TECHNICAL.final §3.9): it follows the Workspace wherever it is placed,
where a Profile decision follows the Profile's current placement. Added
by root-catalog Plan 3.3; every list that carries it defaults to empty,
so a v1 body without it keeps its meaning.

AppleCallbackRequestV1.description:
Apple's `form_post` callback. The same correlation fields as Google's,
plus `user`: the JSON Apple sends, unsigned and only on a person's first
authorization, carrying the name they chose to share. It is a display-name
seed and nothing else.

CloudCatalogBindingRefV2.description:
What the device already records as its account-scope binding
(`Store::bind_account_scope`), if anything. Declared so the service
refuses a device of another account before reading or writing.

CloudCatalogBindingRequestV2.description:
`PUT /v1/account/cloud/catalog/binding`. The account and the identity
come from the native session; the body is only what the device holds.

CloudCatalogBindingV2.description:
The account's one catalog binding (§4.1). A second device, a second
verified identity of the account and a retry all get exactly this.

binding_generation.description:
1 at creation; moves only if the service ever re-mints the scope,
which nothing in this contract does.

CloudCoverageV2.description:
How much of the admitted catalog the projection this receipt was read
from has committed. A count computed under `Partial` is a count of what
the projection has read, not of the catalog; a former Profile is not
declared empty while a unit that may still place something under it is
pending.

CloudDiscoveryCursorV2.description: The cursor of a discovery page: the last Workspace listed.

CloudDiscoveryReceiptV2.description:
`GET /v1/account/cloud/discovery?scope=…[&after_workspace_id=…]`.
Counts a client derives group by `results[*].placement`; a Workspace
appears once, under its current placement, and the receipt says how
much of the catalog that grouping covers.

authorization_generation.description:
The account's authorization generation the receipt was read under;
a permit from an older generation does not correlate to it.

pass.description:
The service's projection pass that produced the receipt. Monotonic
per scope; a client correlates its own pass to it and never treats
an older pass as newer evidence.

CloudDiscoveryScopeV2.description: What a discovery pass asks about.

oneOf.description:
The Profiles and their lifecycle, with the Workspaces currently
placed under each.
The Workspaces the account may sync, with their placement.

CloudHoldReasonV2.description:
Why a valid unit was held rather than stored or forwarded: the export
boundary's own reasons (§4.3) plus the two hosted preconditions.

oneOf.description:
The Workspace's current placement names a Profile whose unit the
account's catalog does not hold as Cloud-eligible. Send that Profile's
unit first, or the Workspace stays held.
A personal unit whose Workspace catalog unit is not admitted yet.

CloudMembershipV2.description:
The account's membership facts for one Workspace — separate from where
the Workspace is placed. These are what content admission reads.

documents_write.description: The live membership also grants document writes.

CloudProfileResultV2.description:
One Profile in a discovery receipt: lifecycle from its catalog unit,
whether its Identity/Private units are currently eligible (§4.4), and
the watermark the answer was read at.

CloudProfileSelectionRequestV1.description:
Select one exact discovery eligibility pair for the current native device.
The Profile comes from the path; every other identity comes from the
session, never from this body.

oneOf.description:
Completed admission for this device and Profile. It is not possession
of Profile bytes or complete sync; local CRDT inventory is that evidence.

CloudRootCatalogV2.description:
`GET /v1/account/cloud/catalog`: the account's admitted units, with a
digest over exactly them so equal digests end the root exchange. No
name, no scope, no hidden subject.

next.description: The last unit listed iff more follow; explicitly null otherwise.

CloudRootJoinReceiptV2.description:
The service's answer to a push: the join receipt of §4.1 on the account
path. `frontier` is always the frontier Cloud holds after the call.

oneOf.description:
Stored durably at `revision`; the projection advances to it
separately and the watermark says when it has.

redacted_ops.description:
How many historical references the hosted derivation redacted
before storing. A number for the device's log, never a list.

oneOf.description: Ancestors missing: nothing stored; send from `frontier`.
Nothing new; an idempotent re-send.
Valid but not storable now; retried when the hold reason clears.

CloudRootUnitRequestV2.description:
`POST /v1/account/cloud/catalog/units/pull`: ask for one unit from the
device's accepted frontier (its join receipt); the empty vector asks for
a snapshot.

CloudRootUnitStateV2.description:
One admitted unit as the service advertises it: its address, the
frontier Cloud holds (an encoded version vector) and how far the
discovery projection has committed it. The watermark is a per-unit
`i64` — the unit revision the projection has read — never a global
vector (§7.3).

CloudRootUnitUpdatesV2.description:
Bytes of one unit through the export boundary, in either direction: a
derived snapshot or updates since the requested frontier, never raw unit
bytes. On a push the device sends them (`POST
/v1/account/cloud/catalog/units/push`); on a pull the service answers
them with the watermark its projection holds for the unit.

projection_watermark.description:
The service's watermark for the unit on a pull; on a push the device
echoes the last watermark it saw, which the service may ignore.

CloudRouteResultV2.description:
Where the scope's session dials, or why not yet. Mirrors the v1
`DatasetRouteResultV1` without a dataset: the dataset, when there is
one, is on the response beside it.

CloudSyncRouteV1.description: Exact endpoint and its advertised paths, not a signed assignment.

CloudSyncScopeV2.description:
One admission scope (§7.3 "separately versioned user-catalog, workspace,
user-personal and optional Profile Identity/Private admissions, each
with its own eligibility and authority generation"). A token is for one
scope; a device holding several holds several tokens.

oneOf.description: The account's root units: Profile and Workspace catalog units.

One Workspace's content, admitted on Workspace id, membership and
incarnation. No Profile is named and none is required.

The account's personal unit for one Workspace. Follows the
Workspace's policy plus the account's own authorization; no Profile.

One Profile's Identity and Private units, eligible only while a
Cloud-enabled Workspace is currently placed under it (§4.4).

CloudUnitRefV2.description:
One unit of the account's catalog: kind and subject, under the session's
scope. Request-side ids are canonical v4 or the body is refused.

oneOf.description:
The user's personal unit for a Workspace, keyed by the Workspace
alone under the account's scope (§5.1).

CloudWorkspaceCandidateKindV1.description: Fixed discriminator of a Cloud discovery candidate.

CloudWorkspaceCandidateV1.description:
One currently authorized Profile/Workspace eligibility pair. No name,
local-only sibling, route, descriptor or credential appears here.

CloudWorkspaceCandidateV2.description:
One Workspace in a discovery receipt: content identity, the account's
membership, and its placement as the committed projection holds it.
`placement.placement` null is explicitly unassigned.

CloudWorkspaceCursorV1.description: The last returned key of a page, echoed back as `after_*` query values.

CloudWorkspaceDescriptorV1.description:
Identity-only bootstrap facts for one authorized Workspace, including the
manifest's original Store document id retained by the Cloud catalog.
Nothing here names, describes or authorizes content.

CloudWorkspaceDescriptorV2.description:
`GET /v1/account/cloud/workspaces/{workspace_id}/descriptor`:
identity-only bootstrap facts for one authorized Workspace, with its
**placement as a projection of the committed catalog** beside — not
inside — the content identity. Nothing here names a membership Profile,
and an explicitly unassigned Workspace is describable (`placement`
null), which the v1 descriptor could not say.

CloudWorkspacePageV1.description: A bounded discovery page. `next` is explicitly null on the last page.

profile_id.description:
The Profile selected at confirmation time. A changed selection must not
silently authorize the Profile frozen into the candidate.

DeveloperErrorV1.description: Stable developer-facing failure. Clients branch on `code`, never `message`.

retry_after_millis.description: Relative delay, independent of device clock skew. Absent on older hosts.

DeviceAttestationEvidenceV1.description:
Public signed evidence relayed to one enrollment peer. Although it is not
a credential, Debug stays structural so logs cannot accidentally become a
durable copy of the complete enrollment claim.

DeviceOwnershipChallengeResponseV1.description: Opaque, bounded challenge issued after authenticating the registration flow.

accepted_terms.description:
That the person accepted the terms. The *version* is the server's own
configured one; a client-supplied version would let a caller record
acceptance of terms nobody showed them.

address.description: Checked against the challenge, as at `verify`.

code.description:
**The code again, not a token saying it was checked.**

Re-checking here means a password can only be set by somebody who still
holds the code, rather than by anybody holding a flow id that was
verified once. It also means no "proved" marker has to be stored, which
would have been either a schema column or a resealed flow artifact --
state existing only to remember something the caller can simply prove
again.

oneOf.description: Somebody finished a sign-up at this address first. Rare, and honest.

EmailNativeStartResponseV1.description:
Begin an email sign-in from a native client.

The same shape as `GoogleNativeStartRequestV1`, and deliberately so: the
device descriptor, callback port, client state and PKCE challenge are
sealed into the flow here, and everything downstream of the exchange —
device registration, the ownership challenge, Profile selection,
enrollment — is then the Google path unchanged.
What a native client gets back when it opens an email flow.

**Its own type, not `AuthStartResponseV1`, because there is no URL.** That
type carries an `authorization_url` and must: a Google start exists to send
a browser somewhere. An email start sends nobody anywhere -- the app shows
the code screen itself -- so the field had no caller, and a response field
nobody reads is a puzzle for whoever arrives next (D22).

address.description:
Checked against the challenge, so this button cannot be pointed at an
address the flow was not started for.

oneOf.description:
The sixty-second cooldown, which is what stops this button being used
to flood somebody else's inbox.

flow_id.description: The native flow this sign-in belongs to, when the app started one.

EmailSignInResponseV1.description:
**One rejection, whatever was wrong.** A response that distinguished "no
account here" from "wrong password" would answer the question D8 spends a
screen and an email refusing to answer -- and the constant-time verify in
`PasswordHashing::verify` exists so the *timing* does not answer it either.

EmailStartRequestV1.description:
Begin proving an address. **The response is identical for every address**,
which is the whole of D8: a stranger typing addresses into the sign-up box
must not be able to learn whether any of them has a Koru account.

flow_id.description:
The native flow this address belongs to, when the app started one.

A native sign-in begins in the app, before anybody has typed an
address: the device descriptor, callback port and PKCE challenge are
sealed then. This attaches the address to that flow instead of opening
a second one, which is what keeps the device bound to the account that
is about to be created.

address.description:
**The address again, and it is checked against the challenge.**

Every step after `start` re-supplies it, and the server refuses unless
its keyed digest equals the one the code was sent to. That is what lets
a native flow exist before an address does, and it means no step has to
store the address anywhere a later step could disagree with.

EmailVerifyResponseV1.description:
What a code came back as.

The two "already known" outcomes are D8 arriving: they are the first moment
Koru will say that an address is known, and they are reached only by
somebody who has just proved they read that mailbox.

**They are two outcomes and not one because they send the person to
different places.** One has a password already and should sign in; the other
has a Google account and has no password to type. A single outcome meant the
page told somebody who had never used Google to press the Google button.

oneOf.description: Proved, and no account exists at this address. Choose a password next.
Proved, and this address already has a Koru password. Sign in with it.

Proved, and this address already signs in with Google. Increment E1
turns this into a journey; until then it is an honest dead end rather
than a second account.

The challenge is dead. A new code must be requested; this is terminal,
not a slower retry.

GoogleCallbackResponseV1.description:
Callback completion is machine-readable even when verified-email collision
policy requires a second, exact-account authentication. The collision flow
is newly minted by identity resolution; it is never confused with the
already consumed OAuth flow.

GoogleIdToken.description: Raw Google ID token delivered by the native account sheet.

app_link_return.description:
Return through the website's verified App Link rather than a loopback
port: how a phone completes a browser sign-in (RFC 8252 §7.2).

client_state.description:
Opaque BFF correlation value, sealed into the flow and returned only to
the configured fixed BFF callback.

JwkV1.description: Public Ed25519 verification key in RFC 7517/8037 form.

capability_keys.description:
The regional token/capability verification keys: what a device checks
its own sync credential against before it dials a worker. Public keys
only, in a third trust domain; a deployment without capability signing
publishes none.

keys.description:
Access-token verification keys. Existing consumers keep this trust
domain and never treat attestation keys as login keys.

app_link.description:
Deliver to the fixed verified App Link instead of `127.0.0.1:port`.
A phone has no loopback a browser can reliably reach, so it asks for
this at start and `port` is then zero.

NativeSessionInspectRequestV1.description:
Read-only ownership observation authenticated by the current native refresh
secret. It issues no token, extends no expiry, and never accepts a previous
secret. Later operations must authenticate normally.

refresh_token.description: Canonical base64url without padding of exactly 32 current secret bytes.

OAuthClientSummaryV1.description:
Who the assistant is, as far as Koru can tell. A metadata-document client
is `verified` and names its `domain`; a dynamically registered client is
unverified and has no domain. The name is self-declared either way.

OAuthConsentDecisionRequestV1.description:
`POST /v1/oauth/consent`. Approving needs `name` and `access`, and a
decision for every Cloud-syncing Profile. Denying needs neither.

request.description: The signed pending request, from the consent cookie.

workspaces.description:
Grants pinned to a Workspace UUID (root-catalog Plan 3.3). A v1
consent page sends none.

OAuthConsentDecisionResponseV1.description:
Where the browser goes next: the client's redirect URI with `code`,
`state` and `iss`, or with `error=access_denied`.

OAuthConsentProfileV1.description:
One active Profile of the account, as the consent view and the
connections list carry it.

name_snapshot.description: The account's discovery snapshot; absent shows "Unnamed Profile".

request.description: The signed pending request, from the consent cookie.

profiles.description:
Every active Profile. Only the Cloud-syncing ones are offered; none
syncing is case (c).

requested_access.description:
What the assistant asked for. Read & edit is preselected only when it
asked for it.

PasswordRefusedV1.description:
Why a password was refused, in terms a surface can show *before* the next
attempt rather than as a bare rejection.

ProfileAccessV1.description: The person's choice for one Profile.

ProfileId.description: ProfileId — a client-minted v4 UUID, hyphenated and lowercase. Immutable, and never derived from a name or a path.

auth_identities.description:
Auth Identities authorized for this Profile. Filled by Profile listing;
mutation responses may return an empty list and clients then refresh.

koru_identity_id.description: Canonical hosted owner used only by targeted acknowledgements.

lifecycle_revision.description:
Current hosted compare-and-set revision. Absence in an older response is
the initial active revision.

name_snapshot.description: Discovery snapshot only; local Profile CRDT data is authoritative.

RefreshIdempotencyKey.description: Canonical base64url-no-pad encoding of exactly 32 random bytes.

enrollment_protocol_version.description:
Enrollment protocol spoken by this build. Old clients omit it and are
deliberately not returned as automatic-enrollment candidates.

auth_identity_id.description:
The exact Auth Identity that authenticated this session. This is an
opaque identifier, not an email or provider subject.

SubjectLifecycle.description:
A subject's lifecycle as the unit's facts reduce it (§4.2: deleted while
a deletion id is named by no restore; purge evidence is terminal).

SyncTokenRequestV2.description:
`POST /v1/account/cloud/sync-token`. Everything but the scope comes
from the native session.

UpdateAppConnectionRequestV1.description:
`PATCH /v1/account/connections/{connection_id}`. At least one change.
Widening to Read & edit reaches the assistant when it next connects; the
tokens it holds keep the ceiling it was approved with.

workspaces.description: Writes a row for every Workspace it names; the others keep theirs.

WorkspaceId.description: WorkspaceId — a client-minted v4 UUID, hyphenated and lowercase. Immutable, and never derived from a name or a path.

WorkspacePlacement.description:
Where a Workspace is placed, as the hosted side projects it. Carried on
the v2 descriptor and the v2 candidate beside — never inside — the
membership facts.

placement_revision.description:
The unit revision at which this placement was committed to the
projection; a Profile-grant cache invalidates on it.

info.description: Account, sign-in, device and Cloud Workspace routes served by the hosted Koru Cloud. The desktop API gateway does not serve them. Errors are { code, message }, where `code` is a stable machine-readable token and `message` is untranslated developer text that must not be shown to a person.
